proposal.analysis: The clearest novel pattern is whole-line denial where a covered repair or replacement is mixed with an upgrade or unrelated work, although the covered baseline can still be valued. A separate failure prices a named multi-component replacement as though it contained only its cheapest component; several other failures instead contradict instructions already present and do not support an additional rule.

rules.rule: When one line includes a covered repair or like-for-like replacement together with a stated upgrade, greater capacity, betterment or unrelated add-on, assess the covered baseline component as covered and related and exclude only the incremental upgrade/add-on cost; do not reject the entire line solely because it contains that component.
rules.hypothesis: This preserves payment for the necessary underlying air-conditioning replacement and covered cellar repair labour while excluding only betterment or unrelated work.
rules.risk: Could over-allow a baseline where the invoice gives no credible way to distinguish it from an entirely elective upgrade, so the estimate must remain limited to a demonstrable like-for-like baseline.

rules.rule: For a replacement line that expressly names several distinct components, price one cheapest reasonable replacement for each named component, plus indispensable fitting labour where inherent to the item; do not value the whole line as only its cheapest named component.
rules.hypothesis: This would value the billiard cloth, cue sets and lighting fixture as separate stated replacements rather than allowing only a basic cloth/accessory amount.
rules.risk: Could raise estimates for loosely worded bundled lines if words describe alternatives rather than separate supplied components; apply only where the line plainly requires all named components.
